audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].side ('Akshan') disagreed with win[5] ('Aurelion Sol') and phases[6].side ('Skill') disagreed with win[6] ('Aurelion Sol') — two rows rendering two answers.
audit.why: The scaling rows belong to Aurelion Sol; the content layer already said so.
audit.corrected: Both full-layer rows flipped to 'Aurelion Sol'. Levels 1-6 left with Akshan — his 850-range Avengerang against a 750-range beam genuinely owns that window, and the 47.07% over 495 games is consistent with a hard lane that scales out.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described as an ally revive; spikes[3] and late claimed a 'global Comet threat', a 'global ultimate' and a '5-star burst'.
audit.why: Comeuppance (R) stores bullets and fires for missing health at 2500 range — it does not revive. The revive belongs to Going Rogue (W), off Scoundrel marks. Aurelion Sol has no global ability and no 'stars' resource beyond stardust; Comet is a rune.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike rekeyed to Comeuppance's real behaviour, first item to Rod of Ages, late to The Skies Descend.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions appeared nowhere: Comeuppance's bullets stop on the first champion, minion or structure hit; Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit; Heroic Swing is knocked off by champion or terrain collision.
audit.why: enemyKit R text ('the first champion, minion, or structure hit'), P flag shield, E text ('gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain'); brief.missingInteractions rule 'shield-absorbs-burst'.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] now tells you to keep a minion between you and the ult; early names the three-hit shield as the thing to force out first; dosFull[1] uses the collision knock-off with Falling Star.

audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, Astral Flight 22s, Falling Star 120s.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three and the collision property.

edits.before: Akshan wins by landing Heroic Swing, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Akshan wins by poking from 850 behind minions, swinging in once you are low, and finishing from 2500 range with Comeuppance.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Astral Flight has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Akshan Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1, and it knocks him off on champion or terrain collision — fight in the window it is down. - Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1: the moment it all goes wrong. - Falling Star: 120s, endings only.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by denying the three-hit Dirty Fighting shield: break the chain by walking out of range, and his poke pattern stops paying him anything.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Akshan for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is his only true escape at 18s, so hold Falling Star for the swing itself — collision knocks him off, and the stun ends the arc.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: His Avengerang shove beats your clear pre-item, and stepping up to contest hands him free ricochet angles through your own caster minions.

edits.before: Comeuppance's revive threat means even a clean kill can be undone, keeping this phase his
edits.after: Comeuppance stores bullets and hits for missing health from 2500 range, ending any retreat

edits.before: Two-item global presence and ultimate burst outscale his marksman-style kit in fights
edits.after: Two items of stardust scaling and black-hole zoning outscale his marksman-style kit

edits.before: Akshan's Going Rogue stealth off cover lets him poke you with Avengerang and vanish before your Comet ever tags him.
edits.after: Going Rogue camouflages him off cover, so Avengerang chips you and he is gone before your 750-range beam can answer.

edits.before: Comeuppance can revive a dead ally mid-fight, meaning even a clean kill from you can be undone if you don't zone the ult range.
edits.after: Comeuppance locks on from 2500 range, scaling with your missing health, but the bullets stop on the first thing hit — stay behind a minion.

edits.before: Your completed core item's burst finally out-trades his auto-poke pattern once he has to step into your Q arc to farm.
edits.after: Rod of Ages plus stardust ticks finally out-trade his auto-poke once he must step into your 750 beam arc to farm.

edits.before: Your global Comet threat and 5-star ultimate outscale his single-target marksman kit entirely once teamfights start.
edits.after: Stacked stardust and The Skies Descend outscale his single-target marksman kit entirely once teamfights start.

edits.before: Akshan's Avengerang ricochets through the minion wave for free poke damage while he stays out of your Q's effective range, and Going Rogue stealth near cover lets him reposition for follow-up autos you never see coming. You lack the early burst to punish his hit-and-fade pattern, so every trade favors him unless he overextends into your zone. Stand behind your wave, don't feed him free ricochet angles, and save your stars rather than forcing bad trades.
edits.after: Avengerang extends its range off every enemy it clips, so he pokes from 850 while your beam only reaches 750, and Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit — force that shield out before you commit anything. You lack the early burst to punish his hit-and-fade pattern, so every trade favors him unless he overextends into your zone. Stand behind your wave, deny him ricochet angles, and save your stars rather than forcing bad trades.

edits.before: Comeuppance is a marksman-style execute ultimate that can also revive a dead ally, so even winning a skirmish against him doesn't guarantee the kill sticks if a teammate died nearby. You're still playing reactive here, using minions and terrain to block his ricochet poke while waiting for your item spike. Ward around brush he uses for Going Rogue resets and avoid giving him isolated pick opportunities before level 6 all-ins resolve.
edits.after: The revive is Going Rogue, not Comeuppance: kill the Scoundrel who killed your ally and he resurrects them, so a won skirmish can still unwind on you at the worst moment. You're still playing reactive here, using minions and terrain to block his ricochet poke while waiting for your Rod of Ages spike. Ward the brush he stealths from and avoid giving him isolated picks before level 6 all-ins resolve.

edits.before: Once your first core item completes, your Q-W combo finally punishes him for stepping up to farm or poke, since he now has to respect your range instead of freely bouncing Avengerang. By two items your global ultimate threat and 5-star burst dwarf his marksman scaling, letting you zone lane and swing fights from across the map. Play around vision on his stealth angles and force him to commit before you engage.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages completes, a held beam off Astral Flight punishes him for stepping up to farm, since he now has to respect your range instead of freely bouncing Avengerang. By two items The Skies Descend and your stardust curve dwarf his marksman scaling, and Heroic Swing cannot carry him out of a 1250-range stun. Play around vision on his stealth angles and force him to commit first.

notes: Biggest single error in this matchup: the revive was attributed to Comeuppance (R) in whys[4], spikes[1] and mid. Per Riot's text the resurrection belongs to Going Rogue (W) via Scoundrel marks; Comeuppance is a stored-bullet, missing-health nuke at 2500 range that stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit. All three fixed. wants.you[2] ('Save Comet for punishing his all-in') still treats the Arcane Comet rune as an ability, but the string is under the 25-character floor territory only in spirit — it is prose and I could not rewrite it inside the band without inventing, so it is left; flagging it here.
